finding.claim: POST /checkout charges the amount computed from client-supplied price and qty, with no validation or server-side price lookup, so an attacker can pay arbitrary amounts or submit a negative total.

trace.note: total = sum of client i.price * i.qty, no type, sign, or range checks

finding.guards_checked: None on the path: no type check on items, price, or qty; no sign or range check; no catalog comparison. Sibling /checkout-v2 (cart.js:13) uses server-side catalog prices, so this route is the unfixed one. Auth applied to the route is not visible in this repo, so the attacker is any caller who can reach the route.

verdict.guard_found: none. cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty with no type, sign, or range checks, and cart.js:6 passes that total straight to req.payments.charge. Nothing in cart.js compares against a catalog. Upstream auth and any checks inside req.payments.charge are not visible in this repo. The sibling /checkout-v2 (cart.js:13-16) uses req.catalog.price(i.sku) and is not the route at issue.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches cart.js:4-7: the client-controlled items feed the total at cart.js:5 without validation, the total is charged at cart.js:6, and the response echoes it at cart.js:7. No effective control exists in the route, and any authenticated caller who can reach it (req.user.id implies upstream auth) can underpay or submit a negative total. The one open point is whether req.payments.charge rejects non-positive amounts, which cannot be seen from this repo, so the severity of a negative total is uncertain even though the price-tampering flaw is not.

finding.claim: POST /checkout-v2 can charge NaN or Infinity: a missing, non-numeric, or unknown-SKU qty/price yields a NaN total, and a huge qty overflows to Infinity, and both are passed to charge without a finiteness check.

trace.note: p = await req.catalog.price(i.sku); unknown SKU may yield undefined
Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty)) gives NaN for missing or non-numeric qty; p * NaN or p * huge can yield NaN or Infinity; total += propagates it
NaN or Infinity total passed to payments.charge

finding.guards_checked: Price is server-side from req.catalog.price (SAFE for price tampering). Math.max(1, ...) blocks zero and negative qty (SAFE for those). No isFinite or NaN check, no upper bound on qty, no SKU validation. Impact depends on payments.charge behaviour for non-finite amounts, which is not in this repo, so the severity is uncertain.

verdict.guard_found: none. cart.js:14 `Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty))` does not stop NaN, since Math.max(1, NaN) returns NaN, and it does not cap large values, so Infinity passes through. cart.js:13 `req.catalog.price(i.sku)` has no undefined check, and cart.js:16 `req.payments.charge(req.user.id, total)` receives the total with no isFinite check. The route has no validation or middleware in this file.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches cart.js: line 13 fetches the price, line 14 multiplies it by a Math.max-clamped qty that yields NaN or Infinity for missing, non-numeric, or huge qty, and line 16 passes that total to charge with no finiteness check, so any caller who can reach the /checkout-v2 route (cart.js:10, presumably an authenticated user since req.user.id is used) can trigger it. Whether the resulting charge is harmful depends on payments.charge, which is outside this repo, so the severity is uncertain even though the defect is real.
